Claim 1 (Currently amended): A catheter system for delivering ultrasonic energy to a treatment site within a body lumen, the catheter comprising: a tubular body having a proximal end, a distal end and an energy delivery section positioned between the proximal end and the distal end; a plurality of ultrasound radiating members positioned within the energy delivery section, the plurality of ultrasound radiating members being allocated into electrical groups comprising more than one ultrasound radiating member; wherein the ultrasound radiating members of one electrical group are spatially interdigitated with the ultrasound radiating members of another electrical group, and wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a __non-regular pattern__.

Claim 4 (Currently amended): The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a __non-regular pattern__.

Claim 5 (Currently amended): The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a __different distribution pattern that varies__.

Claim 6 (Currently amended): A system for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the system comprising: a first __ultrasound catheter__ and a second __ultrasound catheter__, each of the first and the second ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section having at least one ultrasound element, the tubular body also including at least one fluid delivery lumen; and a control system that is connected to and configured to operate both the first and the second elongate cores.

Claim 8 (Currently amended): The system of Claim 7, wherein the control system is configured to independently control the ultrasound radiating members on the first and the second elongate cores.
